overall: The AG found the complaint timely, held the Council violated the Open Meeting Law by convening a April 25, 2022 executive session under Purpose 6 with no negotiating position to protect, declined to review the attorney-client privilege claim, and ordered compliance and full release of the executive session minutes.

allegations.summary: Council allegedly met in executive session on April 25, 2022 without a lawful purpose, invoking Purpose 6 for a discussion of a disputed street.
allegations.key_passage: Because deliberations about Coffin Street did not fall within Purpose 6 or any of the other executive session purposes allowed under the Open Meeting Law, the executive session at the April 25 Meeting was convened without a lawful purpose, in violation of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Council allegedly improperly asserted attorney-client privilege in refusing the complainant's requests for the executive session minutes.
allegations.key_passage: The Open Meeting Law does not authorize the Attorney General to determine whether the Council’s assertion of the attorney-client privilege was justified.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, with a caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
Release to the public, within 30 days of the letter, the minutes of the April 25 executive session in their entirety and without any redactions.
remedy_passage: We order the Council’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, and we caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the law. In addition, we order the Council, within 30 days of the date of this letter, to release to the public the minutes of the executive session of the April 25 Meeting, in their entirety and without any redactions.
